app.crashBody: Something on it stopped with an error. The rest of the console still works; reloading usually clears it.
app.staleBody: This tab was opened before the server was upgraded, and the page it asked for no longer exists. Reload to get the new version.
auth.firstRunDesc: Choose the administrator credentials for this server. There is no account recovery, so store them somewhere safe.
auth.setupCodeHint: The server printed it when it started, and saved it in the file setup-code in its data directory. On a Linux install: sudo journalctl -u polyemesis | grep -A2 'setup code', or sudo cat /var/lib/polyemesis/setup-code. In Docker: docker logs polyemesis, or docker exec polyemesis cat /data/setup-code.
auth.sessionEnded: Your session has ended. Sign in again to continue.
auto.blockDestinationsUnknown: Waiting for the destination list. Until it arrives, leaving this empty would mean every destination — which is not a choice anyone made.
auto.blockRunAtPast: That time has already passed, so this would never fire. Choose one in the future.
auto.blockRunAtUnset: Choose when this fires. A one-shot with no time saves happily and can then never run.
auto.broadcastFault: Broadcast could not be started or ended
auto.coalesced.hint: Repeat alerts folded into one delivery instead of being sent separately, so a flapping destination cannot flood an endpoint.
auto.deleteRuleDesc: The rule stops firing. Its webhook endpoint is untouched, and you can recreate the rule.
auto.deleteScheduleDesc: The schedule stops running. Anything it already started is unaffected.
auto.deliveryUnread: Delivery figures could not be read. These are not zeros.
auto.destinationHeld: Destination held: retries stopped until Retry
auto.dropped.hint: Alerts discarded without being attempted, because the queue was already full. The endpoint is far behind rather than merely slow.
auto.failed.hint: Alerts that exhausted their retries and were given up on. Nothing retries these again on its own.
auto.lastDelivery.hint: When the most recent alert actually reached its endpoint. Long ago, with a non-zero pending count, means deliveries have stalled.
auto.missedNote: An occurrence missed because the server was down is marked handled and skipped rather than fired late — a stream that starts itself four hours late is worse than one that never started.
auto.name: Name
auto.nothingFired: Nothing has fired yet. The scheduler sweeps every 20 seconds.
auto.pending.hint: Alerts waiting to be delivered. A number that only grows means an endpoint is not answering.
auto.retries.hint: Deliveries reattempted after a failure. A few are normal; a climbing count points at a flaky endpoint.
auto.ruleCreated: Alert rule created. Send it a test.
auto.rulesUnread: The alert rules could not be read, so what is configured here is unknown. This is not an empty list.
auto.schedulesUnread: The schedules could not be read, so what is configured here is unknown. This is not an empty list.
auto.secretMasked: Shown masked because the secret lives in the path. Leave it alone to keep the current endpoint, or paste a new URL to replace it.
auto.sent.hint: Alert deliveries this server has completed since it started.
auto.subtitle: Webhooks that tell you something broke, and schedules that run the show without you.
auto.theEndpointDidNotAccept: The endpoint did not accept the test message.
auto.title: Automation
auto.webhookHint: Discord and Slack both give you one under channel settings.
auto.noRules: No alert rules. Add one with a Discord, Slack or plain JSON webhook URL and polyemesis will tell you when a destination drops, the ingest goes away, or the disk fills.
automod.allOrNothing: One pattern that does not compile stops every rule, so the whole save is refused.
automod.answerTimeoutNote: How long to wait for the model, not how long a viewer is silenced.
automod.confidenceOutOfRange: Outside 0.01 to 1. The server would ignore this and use 0.8.
automod.deleteRuleDesc: The pattern stops being checked as soon as the settings are saved.
automod.endpointNote: The chat completions address. An empty one fails every call.
automod.instructionNote: Your own words for what counts as abuse here. Sent with every message.
automod.keyFailed: The key could not be stored: {detail}
automod.keyNeverReturned: The server never returns the key, so it can be replaced but never read back.
automod.maxCallsNote: The spend ceiling, in real money. Zero means no ceiling.
automod.minConfidenceNote: Between 0.01 and 1. A verdict less certain than this is ignored.
automod.modelDesc: An external model, asked only about what the free checkers could not settle. Paid, slow, and never on the hot path.
automod.modelEnabledNote: Off by default. While it is off, no message leaves this server.
automod.modelNoEndpoint: The model checker has no endpoint, so every call fails.
automod.modelOff: The model checker is switched off, so it finds nothing.
automod.nameEmpty: Name this rule. The server names it back when it refuses a pattern, and so does the moderation log.
automod.noRules: No rule is switched on, so this checker finds nothing.
automod.patternEmpty: A rule with no pattern matches nothing.
automod.patternNote: Case is ignored, and padding, homoglyphs and zero-width characters are removed before matching.
automod.rulesDesc: Expressions matched against every message. Free, repeatable, and explainable afterwards.
automod.rulesEmpty: No rules yet, so the rules checker finds nothing.
automod.spendNoCeiling: {used} calls this hour, against no ceiling
automod.spendUnread: Spend could not be read, so this is not a zero.
automod.timeoutZero: A timeout of zero seconds is a permanent ban on every platform. Set a duration.
automod.matrixDesc: What each checker may do, on each platform, without asking. Everything starts off except flagging — nothing here acts until you switch it on.
automod.killSwitchNote: Off stops every automatic action everywhere, whatever the cells below say. Messages are still flagged for review.
automod.irreversibleArmed: An irreversible action is armed. Deleting a message and banning a viewer cannot be undone by polyemesis — a ban needs a human to lift it, and a deleted message is gone from the platform.
automod.noUndoTitle: This cannot be undone by polyemesis
automod.flagRecordedOnly: recorded for review, never acted on
automod.alwaysOnTitle: Every checker's findings are recorded before this matrix is consulted, and recording is all flagging does. There is nothing here to switch.
chatpage.allFiltered: Every platform with messages is filtered out.
chatpage.deleteBody: It is removed on {platform} for everyone watching, and nothing here brings it back. To take it off this pane only — reversible, and invisible to viewers — open the author's card and hide it instead.
chatpage.deleteNote: Deleting removes the message on the platform that issued it. A platform polyemesis cannot delete on says so and names where it can be done instead — the action is never hidden on a guess.
chatpage.droppedTitle: Shown live, but persistence fell behind and the scrollback lost them.
chatpage.dupTitle: The same message seen twice — our own echo, or a platform replaying it.
chatpage.noAccount: Chat is running, but no platform account is attached. Connect one under Settings → Platform credentials.
chatpage.noMatchesInScrollback: No matches in the retained scrollback.
chatpage.notRunning: No chat is running on this server. The scrollback below the timeline is whatever was stored before, and the send box is disabled until a platform is attached.
chatpage.storedTitle: Nothing is attached; this is the stored scrollback.
chatpage.subtitle: Every platform in one timeline, with one send box.
chatpage.title: Chat
chatpage.emptyNotRunning: Chat is not running on this server. Connect a platform account under Settings → Platform credentials, then restart to attach it.
chatpage.emptyNoAccount: Chat is running but no platform account is attached yet.
chatpage.emptyFilteredOne: The platform filter is hiding 1 message. Nothing else has been said. Turn a platform back on above to see it.
chatpage.emptyFilteredMany: The platform filter is hiding {count} messages. Nothing else has been said. Turn a platform back on above to see them.
chatpage.emptyWaiting: Connected and waiting. Nothing has been said yet.
chrome.developmentBuild: Development build {current}. Updates are not offered for builds from source — check the releases page for what has shipped.
chrome.programmeHint: The console follows one programme at a time. Everything on screen describes this one.
chrome.updateAvailable: polyemesis {latest} is available. You are running {current}.
chrome.updateManual: This install is not upgraded from here.
chrome.updateRestartRequired: Ready. It applies on the next restart:
chrome.updateUndone: Previous version restored. It applies on the next restart:
clipedit.clickLine: Click a line to jump there. Select across several and the in and out points move to the words you highlighted.
clipedit.clipThisLineTitle: Set the in and out points around this line
clipedit.copied.hint: How much of the clip is copied straight from the recording rather than re-encoded. Copied video is bit-identical to the source and costs almost no CPU.
clipedit.copiesEveryPacketSecondsBit: Copies every packet. Seconds, bit-exact, and the start snaps back to the nearest keyframe.
clipedit.exportQueued: Export queued. It runs when the machine can spare the cycles.
clipedit.keepsEveryAudioTrackIn: Keeps every audio track in any codec. What the recorder writes.
clipedit.markIn: I — mark in at the playhead
clipedit.markOut: O — mark out at the playhead
clipedit.name: Name
clipedit.noKeyframes: The keyframe positions could not be read, so nobody can say where this cut will really start. It will still work — FFmpeg's own seek lands on a keyframe — but the start may be up to one GOP early and this page cannot show you by how much.
clipedit.noTranscript: Nothing has been transcribed for this recording yet. Each microphone was recorded on its own track, so transcribing it gives you speaker names without a diarization model — and then you can clip by what was said.
clipedit.pickAtLeastOneAudio: Pick at least one audio track, or take all of them.
clipedit.queueNote: The export is queued, not run here: it yields to the live stream, so a cut taken mid-broadcast waits rather than stealing the cycles the stream needs.
clipedit.reEncodesOnlyTheLeading: Re-encodes only the leading part-GOP so the start is exact. The rest is still copied.
clipedit.reencoded.hint: How much of the clip must be re-encoded to put the edges exactly where you asked. Only the re-encoded parts lose quality.
clipedit.shortcuts: J / K / L shuttle, I and O mark in and out, arrows nudge 33 ms and shift-arrows a second. The fine step is one frame at 30 fps; this recording's real rate is not indexed, so it is named in milliseconds rather than guessed at.
clipedit.startMoved.hint: How far the start had to move to land on a keyframe. Copying video without re-encoding can only cut at one, so an unlucky mark moves by up to a whole GOP.
clipedit.starts.hint: Where the finished clip begins in the recording, after snapping to a keyframe.
clipedit.thatCutCouldNotBe: That cut could not be planned.
clipedit.thatIsNotARecording: That is not a recording id.
clipedit.title: Clip editor
clipedit.whatASocialPlatformWill: What a social platform will accept. Fewer codecs survive it.
clips.bitrate.hint: Bitrate of the buffered video, which is what decides how many seconds fit under the memory ceiling.
clips.bufferLiveNote: The buffer switch is a live toggle, not a saved setting: it is off again after a restart.
clips.ceiling.hint: The most memory the clip buffer may use. It drops its oldest video rather than exceeding this.
clips.clipsKept.hint: How many finished clips are being kept on disk.
clips.couldNotChangeTheClip: Could not change the clip buffer.
clips.deleteDescription: A clip is usually the artifact you meant to keep. This removes the file; the recording it came from is untouched.
clips.held.hint: How much of the window is actually filled right now. It fills from zero when a stream starts, so a short hold early on is normal.
clips.inMemory.hint: Memory the clip buffer is currently using for the video it holds.
clips.keyframes.hint: Whether keyframes have been seen in the buffered video. Without them a clip cannot be cut without re-encoding the whole thing.
clips.listUnread: The clip list could not be read. This is not “no clips” — what is on disk is currently unknown.
clips.onDisk.hint: Disk space those kept clips are using.
clips.subtitle: A rolling buffer of what just went out. Capture it after the fact — nothing has to be armed in advance.
clips.theClipDoesNotStart: The clip does not start on a keyframe.
clips.title: Clips
clips.window.hint: How far back the clip buffer reaches. A clip can only be cut from the video still inside this window.
clips.windowAppliesOnEnable: The buffer is off, so there is nothing to apply this to. Turning it on above sends this window with it.
clips.bufferOff: The buffer is off. Turn it on to the right; it costs memory, not disk, until you capture something.
clips.bufferIdle: Nothing is arriving yet. The buffer starts filling as soon as a stream is live.
clips.windowNote: {min}–{max}s. A longer window costs memory proportional to the stream's bitrate.
clips.retention: Retention keeps at most {count} clips and {bytes}; the oldest go first. Clips are MPEG-TS, which every editor and every player opens.
common.allowPrivateTarget: Allow a private or internal address
common.allowPrivateTargetHint: polyemesis refuses to deliver to a LAN, loopback or cloud-metadata address unless you say you meant it. Turn this on for a receiver on your own network; leave it off and a mistyped host cannot be used to probe the machine polyemesis runs on.
dash.audioTracks.hint: How many audio tracks the ingest is carrying. Per-destination mixes select from these, so a number lower than expected means the encoder is not sending them all.
dash.bitrate.hint: Bitrate arriving from the encoder right now. Well below what the encoder is set to send means the network between you is not keeping up.
dash.broadcastEndAccepted: Facebook accepted the end and has not confirmed it yet.
dash.broadcastEnded: Facebook saved this broadcast as a video on demand.
dash.bulkAppliesTo: Applies to all {count} destinations — there is no selection.
dash.bulkResultsEmpty: Results appear here, one row per destination.
dash.bulkStartPartial: {done} of {total} destinations started; the rest are listed below.
dash.bulkStopPartial: {done} of {total} destinations stopped; the rest are listed below.
dash.clipboardUnavailable: Clipboard is unavailable on this origin.
dash.connectPrompt: Connect a YouTube, Twitch, Facebook or Kick account in Settings → Platform credentials to set your stream title, description and category on every platform at once. Each one accepts a different subset — the composer names which, and pushes what it can.
dash.deleteDestDescription: This removes the destination and its routing profile. The platform is untouched, and you can add it back — but the audio routing you set up for it is gone.
dash.deleteDestLive: It is live now: deleting it ends this broadcast.
dash.descTooLong: Too long for {platforms}; that platform will be reported as failed and the others still pushed.
dash.destNoneHere: No destinations on this programme yet.
dash.destOrphaned: These destinations name a programme this server did not list. They are still configured — check whether their source was deleted.
dash.destinationNeedsASource: A destination belongs to a programme, and this install has none yet. Create a source first.
dash.endBroadcastDescription: Facebook stops the live video and saves it as a video on demand. Anyone watching now is disconnected, and the recording stays on the page — the link on this card keeps working. Stopping your encoder ends the broadcast the same way, after about four seconds.
dash.failoverAutoHint: The return mode is automatic, so this comes back once the primary ingest has been delivering steadily. Switching now does not wait for that.
dash.failoverHandBackBody: Your manual choice is cleared. This can change what is on air immediately: with no pin, a slate or a playlist gives way to a live ingest as soon as one is delivering.
dash.failoverHandedBack: The choice is back with the detector.
dash.failoverManualHint: Nothing brings this broadcast back on its own: the return mode is manual, so the standby feed keeps going out until somebody switches it.
dash.failoverPinnedHere: The source is pinned by hand, so the detector is not choosing. It still moves to a standby if this one stops delivering.
dash.failoverPrimaryDown: The primary ingest is not delivering, so the switch is accepted and held until it is.
dash.failoverReturnBody: The feed the platforms are receiving is cut over at once, and viewers see the join. The destinations keep running, so nothing has to be restarted. If the primary ingest is not delivering yet, the switch is remembered and takes effect when it is.
dash.failoverReturnTitle: Put the primary ingest back on air?
dash.ingestPrimaryOffline: The primary ingest is offline. The backup ingest is carrying the broadcast, so bitrate and uptime are not reported for it here.
dash.keyRefreshed: Stream key refreshed from the platform.
dash.laneNoPreview: No preview yet — start your encoder for this programme.
dash.leaveUnchangedNote: “Leave unchanged” sends nothing at all, so the platform keeps what it has. Choosing On or Off writes that value.
dash.loadingDestinations: Checking what this install has configured…
dash.noDestinations: No destinations yet. Add one, then choose which audio tracks it receives.
dash.noEngineRunning: No programme is running, so there is nothing to act on. The sources are still there; their pipelines did not start. The server log says why.
dash.pushStatusLost: The server lost track of this push, most likely because it restarted. Rows that were still pushing may or may not have reached the platform; check there, or push again.
dash.reconnects.hint: How many times the encoder has dropped and come back during this session. Anything above zero points at the network rather than at the server.
dash.stopAllConsequence: Every destination stops publishing and pressing Start all puts the video back. Any YouTube broadcast on this install is ENDED, and a completed YouTube broadcast cannot return to live — starting again streams to a new one you have to create or announce. That is what the per-destination Stop button already does, one row at a time; this does it to all {count}.
dash.streamHealthNoRoute: This server does not expose Facebook stream health yet.
dash.streamHealthNotPublished: This platform does not publish stream health.
dash.streamHealthUnreadable: Facebook sent fields this build could not read: {fields}
dash.subtitle: Ingest once, fan out with shared video and per-destination audio.
dash.title: Dashboard
dash.uptime.hint: How long the current ingest connection has been up. It resets on every reconnect, not when the server restarts.
dash.youtubeStopsAcceptingTheseOnce: YouTube stops accepting these once a broadcast leaves “created” or “ready”.
dash.bulkPacingNote: Starts are spread out rather than fired together, so a long list takes a while and the outcomes below arrive all at once at the end.
dash.noLibsrt: This FFmpeg build has no SRT support, so multi-track SRT ingest will not work. Install a build with {flag}, or switch the ingest to RTMP in Settings.
debug.blurb: Records what the server does into a buffer you can export and send to an engineer. Stream keys and tokens are removed as each line is recorded, not when you export.
debug.confirmBody: This produces a file to send to somebody who does not have this server. Stream keys, tokens and passwords are removed as each line is recorded. The log lines themselves CAN name your destinations, sources and hosts — read the file before you send it. It also carries the polyemesis version and operating system, and no configuration or credentials. The export is recorded in the audit trail.
debug.recordHint: Raises the log level while recording, and returns it afterwards
debug.title: Debug recording
dest.bitrate.hint: Bitrate this destination is sending to its platform right now.
dest.copySourceBody: the source video exactly as your encoder sent it. No encode, no process, no CPU.
dest.dropped.hint: Frames discarded because the platform could not accept them fast enough. Counted for the whole run.
dest.duplicated.hint: Frames FFmpeg padded in because the source was starving, not the platform. Counted for the whole run.
dest.fbBackupHelp: Sends a second copy of this stream to Facebook’s backup ingest, so a dropped connection does not drop the broadcast.
dest.fbBackupReconnect: Turning it on reconnects the stream once — so enable it before you go live.
dest.fbBoxIntro: Sent on the same create call as Audience, so the same rule applies: applied once when the broadcast starts, and left alone entirely if empty.
dest.fbCrosspostHelp: The numeric Page ID from Facebook’s own console (Page settings, or graph.facebook.com/me/accounts while signed in as the Page) — there is no lookup here, so paste the id rather than a name or URL. “Also post” publishes as that Page rather than only sharing the broadcast to it; left off, only the quieter share happens.
dest.fbDonateHelp: Also an opaque id from Facebook’s fundraisers console, not a charity name to search for. Leave blank to attach no donate button at all.
dest.fillFromPlatform: Fill from what this platform publishes
dest.leaveOnFacebook: Leave as it is on Facebook
dest.leaveOnYouTube: Leave as it is on YouTube
dest.muxQueuePair: These are a pair: FFmpeg applies the packet cap only once the queue has grown past the byte threshold, so a threshold on its own does nothing and will be refused. Raise them if a destination reports interleave errors — the audio path here has variable latency, because loudness normalisation reads ahead.
dest.name: Name
dest.restarts.hint: How many times this destination's encoder has been restarted. Above zero means it failed and was brought back.
dest.sourceRequired: Pick which programme this destination carries.
dest.speed.hint: Encoding throughput against realtime. 1.0x is keeping up exactly; below 1.0x this destination is falling behind and will drop frames.
dest.uptime.hint: How long this destination has been connected. It resets on a restart.
dest.variantWarning: Starts a second encode from your source, seeded from “{name}”. It is not a free variation and it does not change what the other destinations on that encode receive. Leave a field blank to keep the source's.
dest.help.rendition: A rendition is one shared encode of the source: a resolution, frame rate and bitrate made once and sent to every destination that picks it. Copying sends the encoder's own video untouched and costs nothing. Encode only when a platform needs a different size or bitrate than your encoder sends.
device.expired: The code expired. Start again to get a new one.
device.startFailed: Could not start the device authorisation.
device.starting: Asking the platform for a code…
device.title: Connect {platform} with a code
empty.dashBody: Nothing is being ingested: this install has no source yet. Create one and this page fills in — preview, ingest URL and destinations.
empty.ingestBody: The listener ports below belong to the whole install and can be set now. Everything else on this tab — the protocol, the credentials and the publish token — belongs to a source, and appears once you create one.
empty.ingestTitle: The ingest belongs to a source
empty.sourcesBody: A source is one ingested programme — one feed from your encoder. Add the first one to begin.
hooks.deleteBody: It stops delivering immediately. The endpoint is untouched, and you can recreate the hook — but its signing key cannot be recovered.
hooks.deliveryUnread: Delivery figures could not be read, so these are unknown. They are not zeros.
hooks.dialogIntro: One signed POST per transition, in order. Unlike an alert, nothing is coalesced or debounced — a script gets every edge.
hooks.empty: No webhooks. Add one and polyemesis will POST a signed JSON body the moment the stream starts or stops, or a destination goes up or down — one delivery per transition, in order, for a script to act on.
hooks.listUnread: The webhooks could not be read, so what is configured here is unknown. This is not an empty list.
hooks.name: Name
hooks.noDeliveries: Nothing delivered yet. Deliveries appear here as transitions happen.
hooks.payloadNote: Payload {version}. Signature in {header}, over the timestamp and body.
hooks.retriesHint: Retries block this endpoint’s own queue, because ordering is the promise. A 4xx is never retried — an endpoint saying the request is wrong will say it again.
hooks.rotateCutover: The new key signs every delivery from the moment you save, so put it in your receiver at the same time or it will reject them.
hooks.rotateHint: Rotate here rather than deleting the webhook and making another: a new webhook starts its delivery numbering again at 1, and a receiver watching for gaps reads that as deliveries it never received.
hooks.rotatePlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current key
hooks.secretTitle: Signing key — copy it now, it cannot be shown again
hooks.statDropped.hint: Deliveries discarded without being attempted, because the queue was full.
hooks.statEndpoints.hint: How many webhook endpoints are configured to receive events.
hooks.statFailed.hint: Deliveries that exhausted their retries and were given up on.
hooks.statQueued.hint: Deliveries waiting to go out. A number that only grows means an endpoint is not answering.
hooks.statRetries.hint: Deliveries reattempted after a failure. A few are normal; a climbing count points at a flaky endpoint.
hooks.statSent.hint: Webhook deliveries completed since the server started.
hooks.testFailed: The endpoint did not accept the test delivery.
hooks.title: Lifecycle webhooks
hooks.triggerBroadcastFault: Broadcast could not be started or ended
hooks.triggersNoneHint: None selected means every trigger, including ones added by a future release.
hooks.urlMasked: The stored URL is never shown in full. Leave the masked value to keep it, or type a new URL to replace it.
jobs.backToDefault: Go back to the default mode for this kind
jobs.broadcastGoing: A broadcast is going out; deferred work yields to it.
jobs.cannotPause: These kinds should be paused but cannot be, so they are finishing instead.
jobs.couldNotReadTheJob: Could not read the job queue.
jobs.cpuSettleHint: How long the load must be calm again before suspended work is released. 0 is not off: the server uses its own 20 seconds.
jobs.cpuSustainedHint: How long the ceiling must be held before work that is already running is suspended, not merely held back. 0 is not off: the server uses its own 30 seconds.
jobs.deferHint: How far ahead blocked work is parked before the governor looks at it again. Short on purpose: the deferral is renewed every tick while the block lasts. 0 is not off: the server uses its own 30 seconds.
jobs.deferred.hint: Jobs held back deliberately, usually until the broadcast ends, so they do not compete with it for CPU.
jobs.deleteDescription: Removes this row from the finished history. This job exported no clip, so nothing leaves the disk.
jobs.deleteExportDescription: This row is the only reference to the clip file this export produced — the download link is keyed on the job — so removing it also DELETES THAT FILE. It is not moved to a bin; it leaves the disk and does not come back.
jobs.deleteTitle: Remove this job from the history?
jobs.failed.hint: Jobs that gave up. These need attention; nothing retries them on its own.
jobs.gpuGateNote: Only kinds marked as using the GPU are gated by this.
jobs.holdDeferredWorkBackOn: Hold deferred work back on a discharging laptop below this. 0 disables it.
jobs.howManyJobsMayRun: How many jobs may run at once. One, because a second transcode buys throughput nobody asked for at a risk nobody accepted.
jobs.ingestLingerHint: Keeps the stream gate shut this long after an ingest stops, so a reconnect is not raced by a transcode pouncing on the gap. 0 opens the gate at once.
jobs.machineSafety: Machine safety. This is the one gate realtime work obeys too.
jobs.noModels: No model files were found in the models directory. Automatic will download the one it picks; naming a specific model here only works once that file exists.
jobs.nothingNewStartsAboveThis: Nothing new starts above this. 0 disables the gate.
jobs.nothingQueued: Nothing queued. Post-production is submitted from the library.
jobs.nothingWasOldEnoughTo: Nothing was old enough to purge. Lower the retention in Policy first.
jobs.purgeDescription: This drops finished jobs older than the retention set under Policy, and DELETES THE EXPORTED CLIP FILES those jobs produced. Those files are not moved to a bin; they leave the disk.
jobs.queued.hint: Post-production jobs waiting for a worker.
jobs.releasedItWillStartAs: Released. It will start as soon as a slot is free.
jobs.retryTitle: Re-arm with a fresh attempt budget
jobs.runNowTitle: Run this one now, ignoring the resource policy
jobs.running.hint: Jobs being worked on right now. The governor caps this so post-production never starves the live stream.
jobs.savedTheConcurrencyChangeTakes: Saved. The concurrency change takes effect when the server restarts — the queue fixes that when it starts.
jobs.stopsEverythingRealtimeIncludedA: Stops everything, realtime included: a CPU that is throttling has already begun degrading the stream. 0 disables it.
jobs.subtitle: Background work: transcription, proxies, thumbnails and archive compression.
jobs.thisManyFinishedJobsSurvive: This many finished jobs survive whatever their age.
jobs.title: Jobs
jobs.whereTheCeilingReleasesThe: Where the ceiling releases. The gap is the hysteresis that stops the gate oscillating.
jobs.whisperMissing: whisper.cpp is not installed here, so this has no effect yet. It is still worth setting: the choice applies as soon as it is.
jobs.windowZoneHint: IANA name, such as Europe/Berlin. Empty means UTC — never the server's own clock.
jobs.yieldNote: Heavy work is queued and yields to the live stream. A dropped frame is unrecoverable; a transcript arriving an hour later costs nothing.
lib.autoGrouped: Grouped automatically. Editing it makes it yours.
lib.autoGroupedNote: This session was grouped automatically. Saving makes it yours, and the grouping pass will stop rewriting it.
lib.clipTitle: Cut a clip from this recording
lib.couldNotLoadTheSession: Could not load the session's segments.
lib.deleteDescription: The file is removed from disk, along with its proxies, thumbnails and transcript. This cannot be undone.
lib.deleteTranscriptDescription: Every segment on this track is removed and stops being searchable. Re-run transcription to try again.
lib.noProxyYet: No proxy yet — open to generate one
lib.nothingRecorded: Nothing recorded yet. Sessions appear as the recorder writes segments.
lib.regroupTitle: Re-runs the grouping. Additive and idempotent: it never merges a grouping you split by hand.
lib.searchPlaceholder: Search everything anyone said, across every recording…
lib.searchableOnly: Segments with a transcript, so they are searchable
lib.subtitle: Every broadcast, searchable. Each microphone was recorded on its own track, so the transcript already knows who said it.
lib.title: Library
lib.transcribeEachTrackOnIts: Transcribe each track on its own — that is what gives speaker attribution
lib.transcribeUnavailable: Transcription is unavailable on this machine, so the captions button on every recording below is greyed out.
media.checkAgainHint: Read this file again and record what it is. Nothing is uploaded; the server reads the copy it already has.
media.checkAlreadyQueued: A re-check of {name} was already queued. It was not asked for twice.
media.checkFailed: Could not queue a re-check of {name}.
media.checkQueued: Queued a re-check of {name}. The result appears here when the job finishes.
media.uploadCancelled: Upload cancelled: {names}. Nothing was stored for it.

media.desc: Upload a file to broadcast from it on a schedule, with no encoder attached. Copy its pull URL into the source's ingest — Settings → Ingest → Pull for the default source.
meters.clip.hint: This track hit 0 dBFS, so samples were lost rather than merely loud. Clipping cannot be undone downstream -- lower the gain at the encoder, not here.
meters.deviation.hint: How far the integrated loudness sits from your target. Positive is louder than the target, which is what a platform will turn back down.
meters.integrated.hint: Loudness over the whole programme so far. This is the figure a platform normalises against, and it needs about 20 seconds before it means anything.
meters.metering.hint: Whether the metering sidecar is running. It reads the relay directly, so these levels are the ingest itself and not any destination's mix.
meters.momentary.hint: Loudness over the last 400 milliseconds. It moves with every syllable, so it is for spotting sudden jumps rather than judging the programme.
meters.monitorOff: The monitor is off. Turn it on to measure what each destination is delivering.
meters.monitorUnknown: Waiting for the analyser's state. The switch stays blank until the server answers.
meters.notUpdatingTitle: {count} consecutive failed refreshes. These readings are as old as the last one that worked.
meters.nothingToMeasure: Nothing to measure yet. Each running destination gets its own EBU R128 analyser on the mix it receives.
meters.range.hint: The spread between the quiet and loud parts of the programme. A very small range sounds flat and over-compressed; a very large one leaves quiet dialogue hard to hear.
meters.shortTerm.hint: Loudness over the last 3 seconds. Steadier than momentary, and the one to watch while mixing.
meters.subtitle: Every channel of every ingest track, straight from the relay.
meters.title: Audio meters
meters.truePeak.hint: The highest instantaneous level, measured between samples the way a decoder reconstructs it. Staying under −1 dBTP leaves room for lossy encoders to overshoot without clipping.
meters.noStream: No stream is arriving. Point your encoder at the publish URL on the Sources page; the track layout and meters appear automatically.
meters.integratedNote: Integrated loudness is the figure a platform normalizes against, and it needs about {seconds}s of programme before it means anything. Until then the verdict is unknown rather than a pass.
meters.defaultTracksNote: No stream is arriving yet, so this shows the default six stereo tracks. The real layout is detected automatically once the encoder connects.
mon.clearedThisDestinationIsBack: Cleared. This destination is back on the generated command.
mon.clearExpertBody: This destination goes back to the generated command. If it is live, its output restarts to pick up the change.
mon.hostCpu.hint: Processor load across the whole machine, not just this server. Encoding is usually what drives it.
mon.ingestLoss.hint: Share of the incoming stream that never arrived. It is measured before anything this server does, so it points at the network or the encoder.
mon.memory.hint: Memory this server process is using.
mon.pid.hint: The operating-system process id, for finding this server in a process list or a log.
mon.relayDrops.hint: Packets the relay discarded because a subscriber could not keep up. Above zero means a destination or the recorder is falling behind.
mon.relayIn.hint: Total bytes the relay has received from the ingest since the server started.
mon.resolveHint: Resolve the command to see exactly what will run before applying.
mon.restarts.hint: How many times a child process has been restarted by the supervisor. Above zero means something died and was brought back.
mon.subtitle: Process health, host resources, and the live FFmpeg log.
mon.title: Monitoring
mon.uptime.hint: How long this process has been running. It resets when the server restarts, not when a stream does.
mon.chooseDestinationToEdit: Choose a destination to edit its command line.
mon.noLogLines: No log lines yet. FFmpeg only writes when something is worth saying.
mon.relayDropsNote: sends to a consumer that had not bound its port yet
play.acrossEveryRungTheBackstop: Across every rung. The backstop that keeps a long run from filling the disk.
play.basicPasswordNote: Players that cannot follow a link (a set-top box, a CDN) can send the same secret as an HTTP basic password instead.
play.boundsTheViewerTableViewers: Bounds the viewer table. Viewers past it are served, just not counted.
play.carriesThePlaybackTokenAnyone: Carries the playback token. Anyone with this URL can watch.
play.clipboardUnavailable: Clipboard is unavailable; select and copy by hand
play.forObsACdnOr: For OBS, a CDN, or any player that speaks HLS.
play.linkReset: New playback link generated. The previous one no longer works.
play.linksProtected: These links only work for a signed-in administrator until you turn on Public.
play.linksPublic: These links work without an account.
play.mustExceedOneSegmentOr: Must exceed one segment, or viewers flicker out between polls.
play.name: Name
play.noCredentialNote: No credential of any kind is required. Only appropriate for a stream you intend the whole internet to see.
play.noRungs: No rungs yet. Add one to publish anything.
play.onDisk.hint: Disk space the playout catalogue is using.
play.oneStereoAacTrackPer: One stereo AAC track per rung.
play.peak.hint: The most viewers connected at once during this session.
play.posterNote: Shown above the video on the public page. The poster is a recent keyframe, refreshed automatically.
play.programmeNote: A viewer has no session and no way to name one in the URL, so this is a stated choice rather than whichever engine happens to run first.
play.protectedNote: Playback is protected by default. Opening it is a separate, deliberate step.
play.removeRungDescription: This rung stops immediately and its segments are deleted. Anyone watching it is dropped; players that can will fall back to another rung. Adding it back is three fields.
play.restartNote: Changing any of these restarts the muxers, which interrupts viewers for a few seconds.
play.rotateDescription: Every link already shared stops working the moment this lands — the player page, the HLS playlist and the embed code — and anyone watching is dropped mid-stream. The old link cannot be brought back.
play.rotateHint: Immediately stops every link already shared. This is how you revoke access.
play.rungNote: Each rung copies its rendition's video bit-for-bit, so adding one costs a muxer and never a second video encode. Only the audio track differs per rung; per-destination routing is untouched.
play.sessions.hint: How many separate viewing sessions there have been.
play.shorterIsLowerLatencyAnd: Shorter is lower latency and more playlist churn.
play.subtitle: Serve the stream to viewers directly, as public HLS.
play.threeIsTheMinimumA: Three is the minimum a player can buffer on.
play.title: Playout
play.watchingNow.hint: Viewers connected to the built-in player right now.
play.audienceDesc: A viewer is counted while they keep pulling segments.
play.offBanner: Playout is off. Nothing is being served to viewers.
play.publicNote: Serve viewers who are not signed in. Off means administrators only, whatever the protection setting says.
play.crossOriginNote: Lets a player embedded on another website fetch the media, and lets this server's player page be framed. Not needed for same-site embedding.
player.missingToken: The link you followed is missing its playback token, or the token has been changed. Ask whoever shared it for a current link.
player.willStart: This page will start playing on its own when the broadcast begins.
preview.startEncoder: Start your encoder to see the preview
playlist.hint: Uploaded in Media. An item this playlist names that later loses its upload shows as needing attention above, rather than failing silently the next time failover reaches it.
playlist.missingUpload: This upload can no longer be found.
playlist.title: Playlist
rec.deleteDescription: The file is removed from disk, along with its proxies, thumbnails and transcript. This cannot be undone.
rec.diskRecordings.hint: How much of that volume this server's own recordings account for.
rec.empty: No recordings yet. Enable recording on the right and start a stream.
rec.free.hint: Space still available. The recorder stops writing rather than filling a disk completely.
rec.haltedDefault: Recording is halted: the volume is below the free-space floor.
rec.haltedRestarts: The recorder restarts by itself once space is freed.
rec.help.enabled: Writes every ingest to disk as it streams, keeping all audio tracks separate and unencoded. Recording is independent of what you send to platforms: turning it off does not affect your live output, and turning it on costs disk rather than upload bandwidth.
rec.help.maxAgeHours: Deletes recordings older than this many hours, whatever the total size. Useful when you only ever need the last day or two. Set 0 to keep everything until some other limit removes it.
rec.help.maxGb: A ceiling on the total size of recordings polyemesis keeps. Once past it, the oldest are deleted until the total fits again. Set 0 for no size limit — in which case age, or the free-space floor, is the only thing bounding growth.
rec.help.minFreeGb: A hard stop: recording halts when the volume drops below this much free space and resumes on its own once space is freed. This is the one limit that accounts for files polyemesis did not write, so it is the setting that actually protects a shared disk from filling up.
rec.help.segmentSeconds: How long each file is before the recorder starts a new one. Shorter segments limit what a crash can cost you and make individual files easier to move, but leave more of them to manage. Cuts land on a keyframe, so the real length varies by a second or so.
rec.help.stemFiles: Also writes each audio track as its own file alongside the master. Useful when you edit afterwards and want the host, the guests and the game audio on separate channels. It multiplies what a session writes by roughly the number of tracks, which is why it is off by default.
rec.help.stemFormat: Both options are lossless, so neither costs quality. FLAC is about half the size and is what you want unless a tool in your workflow cannot read it; WAV opens in anything. Tracks wider than 8 channels fall back to WAV automatically.
rec.listUnread: The recordings list could not be read. This is not “no recordings” — what is on disk is currently unknown.
rec.minFreeNote: The caps above only bound what polyemesis wrote; anything else on the volume can still fill it. 0 = no floor.
rec.retentionNote: Retention runs every 30 seconds: oldest first, by age then by total size. The segment currently being written is never deleted.
rec.stemFlac: FLAC — lossless, about half the size
rec.stemNote: Written from the same process as the master, so every stem stays sample-aligned with the others. Tracks wider than 8 channels fall back to WAV on their own.
rec.stemsTitle: {count} per-track stem files, sample-aligned with the master
rec.stemsUnread: The per-track files could not be listed, so whether this segment has any is unknown.
rec.stemsUsage.hint: Space used by per-track stem files, written alongside the mix so a track can be re-mixed later.
rec.subtitle: The full multitrack archive: every ingest audio track preserved, unencoded.
rec.title: Recordings
rec.unsavedRetention: Unsaved retention numbers. Save the policy to apply them — the switches above save on their own and will not carry these.
rec.used.hint: Space used on that volume by everything on it, not only by recordings.
rec.volume.hint: The filesystem recordings are written to.
rend.aspectBlurpadHint: Fills the remainder with a blurred, cropped-to-fill copy of the frame itself. This is the convention vertical feeds have settled on.
rend.aspectCropHint: Centre-crops to the target shape, then scales. Subjects keep their on-screen size; the edges of the frame are gone.
rend.aspectPadHint: Scales the whole frame to fit and fills the rest with a flat colour. Nothing is lost, but a 16:9 source on a 9:16 canvas is mostly bars.
rend.aspectStretchHint: Scales to the target size and lets the picture distort if the source disagrees. What every rendition did before the other modes existed.
rend.chooseHardware: Choose a hardware encoder, or a smaller output.
rend.costBeyond: Software encoding this in real time is beyond most machines
rend.costBeyondDetail: {label} is {mpps} for a single encode. x264 at this size usually loses the race with real time, and a rendition that falls behind drops frames for every destination reading it — which you find out mid-stream.{machine} {escape}
rend.costBusy: Expect several cores to be busy
rend.costBusyDetail: {label} is {mpps} on {encoder}, which is a heavy real-time encode.{machine} Watch the encoder's speed once it is live: below 1.0× it is falling behind and the destinations under it will start dropping frames. {escape}
rend.costModestDetail: {label} is {mpps}, within reach of most machines.{machine} It is still one real encode — shared by every destination that selects it, but not free.
rend.costNoNumbersDetail: Nothing has probed the source, so “keep source” has no numbers behind it. Start the ingest and this fills in.
rend.costOffloadedDetail: {label} ({mpps}) runs on the GPU's fixed-function encoder, so it costs little CPU. Quality and rate control vary by driver, and every chip has a ceiling of its own — check the output before a show that matters.
rend.created: Rendition created. Select it on a destination to start the encode.
rend.deintAllHint: For sources that are interlaced but do not say so. Plenty of SDI bridges and capture cards flag everything progressive regardless of what they were fed, and on those “only interlaced” is a no-op that looks like a broken setting.
rend.deintAutoHint: Touches only frames the source flagged as interlaced, so progressive frames pass through untouched. The right choice for anything mixed.
rend.deintOffHint: Right for the progressive sources almost everyone has. Deinterlacing one softens it for no gain.
rend.deleteFallbackMany: {count} destinations fall back to passthrough and will be sent the source video unchanged. Check the source still fits what each platform accepts.
rend.deleteFallbackOne: {count} destination falls back to passthrough and will be sent the source video unchanged. Check the source still fits what each platform accepts.
rend.deleteNoDestinations: Nothing selects this rendition, so deleting it changes no destination.
rend.deleteUsersUnknown: The destinations reading this rendition could not be read, so what deleting it changes is unknown. Any that select it fall back to passthrough and are sent the source video unchanged.
rend.empty: No renditions. Every destination is on passthrough, which is exactly right until one of them cannot take the source — a 4K60 ingest that Twitch, Kick or X will not accept, say. Add a rendition and point those destinations at it.
rend.encoderRelatedFailed: {name} was not offered because a related encoder failed here.
rend.encoderTestFailed: {name} failed a one-frame test encode on this machine.
rend.encoderTestOk: {name} encoded a test frame on this machine.
rend.evenNote: 0 on an axis keeps the source's and preserves the aspect ratio — set height alone to rescale. Both must be even numbers: H.264 and HEVC have no odd-sized chroma plane.
rend.gop.hint: Seconds between keyframes. Shorter starts playback sooner and seeks more precisely; longer costs less bitrate for the same quality.
rend.gpuUnopenable: A GPU is present but this process cannot open it
rend.hevcWarning: This encoder produces HEVC. Most RTMP destinations accept H.264 only — pick it only for a destination that has told you it takes HEVC.
rend.live.hint: The bitrate it is actually producing right now. Well below target usually means the encoder cannot keep up.
rend.name: Name
rend.needsBothAWidthAnd: Needs both a width and a height — with one axis free the scale already preserves the aspect ratio.
rend.needsBothAxes: Needs both a width and a height
rend.noEncoder: This FFmpeg reported no usable video encoder.
rend.noHardwareEscape: No hardware encoder works on this machine, so there is nothing to move this onto — the only lever here is a smaller output. Re-detect hardware if you have since installed a driver or passed a GPU into the container.
rend.noProcessToRestart: Nothing to restart: no encode process is reported for this rendition.
rend.notProbed: Nothing has been test-encoded on this machine yet, so this list is what the FFmpeg build contains rather than what the hardware can do. Re-detect to find out.
rend.noteDuplicateFps: The source runs at {srcFps} fps, so {fps} fps only duplicates frames.
rend.noteUpscale: The source is {width}×{height}. Scaling up costs CPU and adds no detail.
rend.percentNote: Everything is a percentage of the frame, so the same settings are correct on a 16:9 tier and a 9:16 one. Margins are ignored on a centred axis.
rend.preset.hint: The encoder speed/quality preset. Faster presets cost less CPU and spend more bitrate for the same quality.
rend.presetStartingPoint: Starting point — verify current limits with the platform.
rend.redetectTitle: Re-run the GPU scan and encode one test frame with each encoder. Takes a few seconds.
rend.redetectedNoHardware: Hardware re-detected. No hardware encoder passed a test encode on this machine.
rend.restartEncode: Restart this encode and the destinations reading it
rend.restarting: {name} is restarting. Its destinations reconnect with it.
rend.seedNote: These seed the form and nothing more — edit anything before saving. Platform ceilings change and differ by partner status.
rend.speed.hint: Encoding throughput against realtime. 1.0x is keeping up exactly; below 1.0x the rendition is falling behind and will drop frames.
rend.subtitle: One shared video encode, many destinations. Audio is never touched here.
rend.target.hint: The bitrate this rendition is configured to produce.
rend.title: Renditions
rend.unused: No destination selects this yet, so nothing is being encoded. Pick it on a destination to start the encode.
rend.uptime.hint: How long this rendition's encoder has been running.
rend.usersNotNamed: The live list has not arrived, so they cannot be named here — the count comes from the stored rows.
rend.usersUnknown: The destinations reading this rendition could not be read.
rend.waitingSnapshot: Waiting for the first live snapshot.
rend.howBody: A rendition re-encodes video only and copies every audio track through it untouched. Destinations still do -c:v copy plus their own routing graph, so per-destination audio keeps working on top of a shared picture and no audio is ever encoded twice. Three destinations that all need 1080p60 cost one encode, not three.
route.audioAndVideoGoOut: Audio and video go out together.
route.audioRoutingDesc: Choose exactly which ingest tracks each destination receives.
route.duckingNoTargetInMix: None of this destination’s mix is in the duck, so nothing here is pushed down. The stored duck still applies wherever its targets are mixed.
route.duckingNote: Pull one group of tracks down whenever another is speaking — the mic over the music bed. Off means every selected track is summed at its own gain, unchanged.
route.duckingTriggerNote: A trigger does not have to be in this destination’s mix — a mic can duck the music here while only the music is sent.
route.everyTrackReaches: Every selected track reaches this destination, music included.
route.keepMusicOut: Keep music out of this destination
route.localOnlyNote: This server does not store track roles yet, so these stay in this browser. Everything else on the page saves normally.
route.measuredOverTheWholeProgramme: Measured over the whole programme, not moment to moment: quiet passages stay quiet. These are the numbers the platforms' own normalizers aim at, so hitting one is what stops the platform turning you down.
route.presetApplied: Preset applied. Review it, then save.
route.rolesNote: Roles describe the ingest, not this destination, and save on their own. Nothing is filtered until a destination below asks for it.
route.targetFollowsPreset: The target follows the preset above. Choose “Custom…” to type your own.
route.title: Routing
route.withoutATargetTheMix: Without a target the mix goes out at whatever level the ingest produced, with only the clip protection above applied.
route.vodConfigured: A second mix is configured for this destination
route.vodNote: A whole second mix of the same ingest, intended for a second audio track alongside the live one. The usual reason is an archive that must not carry licensed music while the live mix does. Off is the normal state.
route.vodRestores: Switching this back on restores the mix you just turned off.
route.copyFooter: Video is copied without re-encoding. Only this audio graph is applied, and saving affects only this destination: a change to levels alone applies live where supported, anything else restarts it.
route.videoHeldBack: Video is held back {ms} ms at the input to let the audio run ahead.
set.acmeCheckName: A name a public CA can issue for
set.acmeEmailHint: Goes in the file below and nowhere else. Let's Encrypt requires one for expiry warnings.
set.acmeIssuing: Let's Encrypt has been asked for a certificate and there is not one yet. The checks below say what is standing in the way.
set.acmeOwnCert: This certificate is yours to renew. Let's Encrypt would take that over — the checks below say whether this host could get one.
set.acmeProxy: A reverse proxy in front of this box terminates TLS, so the certificate is its business rather than this server's. Configure it there.
set.acmeRateLimit: Let's Encrypt limits failed attempts to five per hostname per hour. Clear what is flagged before restarting, or the next try is an hour away.
set.acmeReady: Nothing this server can see would stop issuance.
set.acmeSwitchable: Browsers do not trust this server's certificate. If this box has a public DNS name and port 80 reaches it, one they do trust is a few lines of config away.
set.acmeThen: Write this to config.yaml, then restart:
set.acmeTrusted: Let's Encrypt issued this certificate and renews it automatically. Nothing to do here.
set.alertDeliveryDesc: How hard a webhook that is not answering gets chased, before the alert is given up on.
set.apiTokensDesc: Long-lived credentials for scripts, Prometheus and anything else that cannot hold a session. Send one as Authorization: Bearer pmk_…. No token can manage tokens, change the password or upload media — those stay behind the password, so revoking one is final.
set.attemptsBackoff: The wait between attempts backs off automatically to a 30 second ceiling, so the top of this range is already several minutes of chasing one dead endpoint. Bounded is the point — retrying forever turns a single dead webhook into a queue that never drains.
set.attemptsNote: Including the first try. 1 means never retry.
set.attemptsRetryable: Only failures worth retrying are retried. A 404 from a webhook somebody deleted is permanent, and trying it again four times only delays every alert queued behind it; a 502 from a reverse proxy is exactly what these attempts are for.
set.brokerPlainNote: mqtt:// is unencrypted. MQTT sends the username and password in its CONNECT packet, so both cross the network in the clear — fine on a trusted LAN, which is the usual Home Assistant case, and not fine over anything you do not control. Use mqtts:// if the broker offers it.
set.brokerUrlNote: mqtt://, mqtts://, ws:// or wss://. A password in the URL is refused: a URL reaches log lines and ps output, and there is no taking it back. Put it in the field below, where it is encrypted at rest.
set.chatBothApply: Both apply and the more generous one wins: a message goes when it is older than the hours and outside the newest N. So a busy channel keeps less time than a quiet one at the same settings.
set.chatFloorWhy: That is the right way round: the floor is what stops a slow channel's user cards being empty.
set.chatBufferNote: Send on connect is a different kind of number from the other two. Those bound what is kept on disk; this one is a buffer held in memory, allocated per connected dashboard.
set.chatHistoryDesc: How far back the chat scrollback goes — and with it, how much a moderator can see when they open somebody's card.
set.chatNotOnlyDisk: This is not only a disk setting. Clicking a name in chat opens what that person has said before, and that history comes from here — no platform publishes an API for it, so polyemesis can only show what it kept. Set this too short and somebody who has been trouble for a week reads as though they have never said anything.
set.chatPurgeNote: How promptly a message past the limits above actually leaves the database. It is one indexed delete, so this is about promptness rather than load.
set.chatSmall: Chat is small. A channel averaging ten messages a second stores roughly 7 MB an hour; most are nowhere near that.
set.chatYouTubeQuotaNote: Units per day for this install's Google Cloud project. A default project gets 10,000; raise this only if a YouTube API Services audit granted you more. Too low just slows chat — too high makes it stop mid-broadcast until midnight Pacific.
set.chatYouTubeReserveNote: Taken out of the allowance above and kept for posting, so that a day of reading chat can never leave a moderator unable to speak. At most half the allowance: more than that leaves too little to read with.
set.clientIdNote: Must be unique on the broker. A collision is the number-one cause of an unexplained reconnect loop: the broker disconnects the older session on every connect, and both clients reconnect forever.
set.couldNotReadTheTls: Could not read the TLS status.
set.couldNotSaveTheMqtt: Could not save the MQTT settings.
set.disconnectDesc: Destinations using it keep their settings but stop refreshing their stream key. You can reconnect the same account afterwards.
set.displayDesc: How times are written down, everywhere in this console. Presentation only: it changes nothing about when anything happens.
set.displayTimeZoneNote: An IANA name. Empty means UTC — deliberately not the browser's own zone, so that two people on the same production read each other's screenshots the same way. Schedules are unaffected: a schedule states its own zone or means UTC.
set.displayTimeZoneUnknown: This browser cannot resolve that zone. The server has its own zone database and may accept it anyway, but check the spelling first.
set.drawtextMissing: This build has no drawtext filter, so text overlays are unavailable. It needs an FFmpeg built with libfreetype.
set.drawtextOk: This build can draw text on video.
set.failoverDesc: A standby input and a holding card, for when the live source stops delivering. Off by default: with it off the pipeline is byte-for-byte what it was before this existed.
set.failoverRemuxNote: Turning this on adds one remux hop between the ingest and everything below it. Cheap, but not free, which is why it is a decision rather than a default.
set.ffmpegUnknown: Could not read what FFmpeg on this box can do.
set.goingLiveDesc: What happens when several destinations start at once.
set.graceNote: How long the live source may deliver nothing before the tier switches. Longer than a reconnect on purpose — an encoder re-establishing an RTMP connection is normal operation, not a failure.
set.ingestDesc: SRT carries up to 32 audio tracks. RTMP carries one, and exists as a fallback for encoders that cannot do SRT. Pull dials a source instead of waiting for one.
set.intervalNote: Unchanged state is not republished, so a short interval costs a comparison rather than a message. The keep-alive is what bounds how long a dead link goes unnoticed — and therefore how quickly the broker tells subscribers this instance is gone.
set.listenersDesc: Where the server binds, for the whole install. One SRT port serves every source — they are told apart by their publish token, so adding a source never means publishing another port. RTMP works the same way, with the stream key as the address, so its port serves every source too.
set.logsBoundNote: The log directory is bounded by the product of these two, so persistence can never be the thing that fills the disk.
set.logsDesc: Captured FFmpeg stderr is always kept in memory, but that dies with the server — which loses exactly the lines explaining why it died. Persisting mirrors it to a rotating file under the data directory.
set.metersDesc: One sidecar process meters every channel of every track. Lower intervals update faster and cost more CPU.
set.modePull: Pull — dial a camera, feed or file
set.mqtt5OnlyNote: A broker pinned to 3.1.1 will not complete a connection at all — it is not a degraded mode. Mosquitto 2.x, EMQX and the Home Assistant add-on all speak 5.0.
set.mqttDesc: Publishes state to a broker as retained messages, so a consumer that was not connected when something changed still gets the current answer.
set.multiAccountNote: Connect the same platform more than once to stream to multiple channels — each account becomes its own destination.
set.name: Name
set.noEncryption: Nothing is encrypting this connection. Passwords and session cookies cross the network in plaintext — set tls.mode: auto, or bind to 127.0.0.1 behind a proxy.
set.noLibsrt: This FFmpeg build has no SRT support. Install one configured with --enable-libsrt, or use RTMP.
set.passphraseNote: Enables AES encryption. Leave blank for none. SRT rejects passphrases outside 10–79 characters.
set.passwordMismatch: The new passwords do not match.
set.passwordNote: The password is never returned by any API, so this box is blank even when one is set. Leave it empty to keep the stored password; clear it with the button below.
set.pipelineOneSave: One Save for this tab: it commits every card here, the broker password included.
set.platformReadFailed: The stored platform credentials could not be read, so the setup forms are withheld. An empty form drawn over a working credential is how a client secret gets regenerated for no reason.
set.platformsDesc: Platforms differ in how much of this polyemesis can automate, and the difference is worth knowing before you start rather than an hour in. Streaming itself works the same everywhere — per-destination audio routing, renditions, reconnect and meters do not depend on any of the columns below.
set.playLoop: Play a loop when nothing is live
set.playLoopNote: A second candidate beside the slate: files play instead of a still image. Both can be on -- see the tier order in the Failover design for which wins.
set.previewDesc: The dashboard's HLS monitor. This is the only place polyemesis re-encodes video, and it runs on its own relay subscription so it can never affect a destination.
set.previewIdleNote: The encoder starts when the dashboard asks for the playlist and stops again this long after the last request, so a closed dashboard costs no CPU. Changing this never restarts a preview someone is watching.
set.proxyTerminatesTls: A reverse proxy in front of polyemesis terminates TLS, so this server serves plain HTTP on purpose.
set.reconnectCapNote: 0 uses the default. HTTP and HLS sources only.
set.redirectNote: Must match exactly, including scheme and port. If you reach polyemesis through a reverse proxy, use that public URL.
set.removeCredsDesc: Every account connected through this app stops refreshing its token and will need reconnecting. The client secret is not recoverable from here — you would create a new app at the platform.
set.returnAutomatic: Automatic — return once the primary is steady
set.returnManual: Manual — stay on the backup until I switch
set.returnManualNote: Manual is the default because an automatic return can flap: a primary that is recovering in bursts would move the programme back and forth mid-broadcast.
set.revokeTokenDesc: This cannot be undone. The plaintext exists nowhere any more — not here, not on the server — so anything still holding this token starts being refused at once and cannot be given it back. Issue a new token instead.
set.rtspNote: TCP unless the camera cannot. RTSP over UDP through NAT looks connected and delivers nothing.
set.saveAndDrop: Save and drop the live stream
set.settingsSavedAffectedProcessesHave: Settings saved. Affected processes have been restarted.
set.showSlate: Show a slate when nothing is live
set.slateBitrateNote: A floor rather than a budget: a still frame needs almost nothing, but platforms watch for a bitrate before they call a stream unhealthy. 0 takes the default.
set.slateColourNote: One word, because it lands on a filter graph where a comma would end the argument. Used only when no image is set.
set.slateEncoderNote: Empty is libx264, and that is the right choice even on a machine full of hardware: a still frame costs a software encoder nothing, and the slate's one job is to start when everything else has already failed. An encoder this FFmpeg build cannot use falls back to software and says so in the log. The preset vocabulary belongs to the encoder — veryfast for x264, p4 for NVENC.
set.slateImageNote: A path inside the data directory. Leave it empty to paint a flat colour instead — that is the fallback precisely because a colour has no file that can fail to open.
set.sourceUrlNote: One of {schemes}. A file:// source is a path RELATIVE to the data directory and may not contain ".." — it is confined there the same way a file upload is.
set.staggerNote: 0 is off. Going live otherwise means every destination opening a connection, negotiating TLS and starting to encode audio in the same tick — on a small box that is the moment most likely to drop frames, and it is the exact moment you are watching, because it is when you went live. A few hundred milliseconds is plenty.
set.staggerReconnectNote: It never delays a reconnect. A destination that drops at 3am comes back immediately rather than waiting its turn behind processes that are already healthy.
set.streamKeyNote: Publishers must use this exact path, so an open port is not an open door.
set.subject: Subject
set.synthesiseNote: Every major platform rejects a stream with no audio track. With this on, a video-only ingest gains one silent stereo track and its destinations start; with it off they refuse with "routing profile selects no audio". It only ever applies to an ingest that PROBED with zero tracks, so it can never displace audio you are actually sending.
set.syntheticDesc: What happens when the ingest carries video and no audio at all.
set.title: Settings
set.tlsDesc: Configured in config.yaml, not here — TLS must be right before the server starts listening. This card reports what that produced.
set.tokenHashNote: polyemesis stores only a hash. If you lose it, revoke this token and create another.
set.tokenScopeAdminHint: Can do everything the admin can, apart from managing tokens, changing the password, uploading media, staging an upgrade and exporting a debug bundle. Only mint one of these if something genuinely has to make changes unattended.
set.tokenScopeReadHint: Can read anything the console shows — status, stats, metrics, the media list — and cannot change a single thing. This is what a monitoring script wants.
set.tokensUnread: The token list could not be read. This is not “no tokens” — who can reach this server over the API is currently unknown.
set.topicPrefixNote: Separators in the prefix are preserved, so home/av means two levels. A prefix starting with $ is refused: brokers reserve those, and a subscriber using # never receives them — the telemetry would publish successfully and be invisible in exactly the view you would debug with.
set.whyDevApp: Why you need your own developer app
set.whyDevAppDesc: polyemesis cannot ship OAuth client secrets — anyone with the binary would have them, and the platforms would revoke them. You register a free developer app once, paste the client ID and secret here, and polyemesis then fetches your stream keys for you.
set.ebDesc: What this machine's GPU is, for the negotiation a destination with Enhanced Broadcasting switched on makes at go-live.
set.ebExperimental: An inventory declared here does reach Twitch's live endpoint, and polyemesis's own tests watch it be accepted: a supported GPU is granted Enhanced Broadcasting, a VOD audio track and a minted key. What Twitch checks is this declaration — the vendor ID, device ID and driver version as sent, against a list it does not publish. It has no way to inspect the machine, which is why these fields exist at all: polyemesis sends what it is told. What has never been observed is a broadcast published through a minted key. Filling this in is safe either way — nothing is sent until a destination with the toggle on goes live, and a refusal falls back to the ordinary Twitch ingest.
sources.addDescription: One ingested programme, with its own ingest, destinations and renditions. A second one is a separate canvas alongside the first — a vertical beside a horizontal, say. Both arrive on the same listener ports and are told apart by their publish tokens.
sources.added: Added “{name}”. Set its ingest ports below.
sources.defaultDescription: Requests that do not name a source act on this one.
sources.deleteDescription: Its destinations and renditions go with it — they describe where this programme goes and mean nothing without it. Recordings are kept: the files are still on disk and still playable, they just stop being attributed to a source.
sources.deleteLastDescription: This is the only source on this install. Deleting it leaves no programme at all — nothing to publish to and nothing to send on — until you add another from this page.
sources.deleted: Deleted “{name}”, its destinations and its renditions
sources.deletedLast: Deleted “{name}”, its destinations and its renditions. This install has no programme now.
sources.dirtyIdle: Unsaved ingest changes. Applying restarts this source's ingest.
sources.dirtyPublishing: An encoder is publishing to this source. Applying restarts its ingest and drops everyone watching.
sources.help.app: The RTMP application path — the part of the URL between the host and the stream key. Most encoders expect “live”. Change it only if you have a reason to.
sources.help.ingest: How your encoder reaches this source. SRT survives a lossy connection by retransmitting what went missing, and is the right default over the public internet. RTMP is older and universally supported, but it degrades badly on an unstable uplink. Pull makes polyemesis fetch from a URL you provide instead of waiting to be published to.
sources.help.latencyMs: How long SRT will wait for a late or retransmitted packet before giving up on it. Higher values ride out worse connections at the cost of delay: roughly 2.5× your round-trip time is a good starting point, so a 40 ms RTT wants about 100 ms here. Too low and a brief hiccup becomes a visible glitch.
sources.help.passphrase: Encrypts the SRT connection, and today this is what actually keeps strangers out of this ingest. Between 10 and 79 characters. Leave it empty and anyone who can reach the port can publish to it.
sources.help.streamKey: The secret an encoder sends to publish over RTMP. This is the credential that gates this ingest, so treat it like a password: anyone holding it can broadcast to your destinations.
sources.help.token: Identifies this source when several share one ingest port. Whether it also gates access depends on your ingest mode — the note underneath says which is true right now. Rotating issues a new token and keeps the old one valid for five minutes so a live encoder is not cut off mid-broadcast.
sources.name: Name
sources.noEngine: No engine is running for this source. The usual cause is an ingest port already in use by another source or another process.
sources.ownDescription: Its own destinations, renditions and recordings.
sources.rotateIdle: A new token is issued immediately. The old one keeps working for five minutes so an encoder already using it is not cut off.
sources.rotateWhilePublishing: An encoder is publishing to this source right now. The old token keeps working for five minutes, so it will not be cut off — but it must be updated before that window closes.
sources.subtitle: One ingested programme each. Destinations and renditions belong to a source.
sources.title: Sources
sources.tokenEnforcedDetailRtmp: It is the stream key: publish to the URL above with this as the key. Rotating issues a new one and keeps the old working for five minutes, so you can move across without dropping a live stream.
sources.tokenEnforcedDetailSrt: Put it in your encoder's SRT streamid to publish to this source on the shared port. Rotating issues a new one and keeps the old working for five minutes, so you can move across without dropping a live stream.
sources.tokenNotEnforced: This token is stored but not enforced right now.
sources.tokenNotEnforcedRtmp: The shared RTMP port is not listening, so no encoder can publish to this source. The listener status and the server log say why.
sources.tokenNotEnforcedSrt: The shared SRT port is not listening, so no encoder can publish to this source. The listener status and the server log say why.
sources.tokenUnusedPull: This source pulls its stream from the URL above, so no encoder publishes to it and the token is not used.
sources.tokenUnusedUnset: No ingest protocol is chosen for this source yet, so every publish with this token is refused. Pick SRT or RTMP above.

tour.addDestination.body: A destination is one place this install publishes to: a platform, a plain RTMP or SRT endpoint, or a file. Choosing a known platform fills in its ingest server, its encoder ceilings and its codecs, so there is no URL to look up. Stream keys are encrypted before they are stored, with a key file that lives outside the database — which is what the last step of this tour is about.
tour.addDestination.title: Add a destination
tour.addSource.body: A new install has no sources — nothing is created for you. Add one here, choose SRT or RTMP, and the exact address to paste into your encoder appears on that source's card, together with the token that addresses it. SRT carries the token in the streamid field; RTMP splits into a server URL and a stream key, which is the two-box form OBS asks for.
tour.addSource.title: Create your first source
tour.dataDirectory.body: Everything this install stores lives in this directory: the database, the recordings, and secret.key. secret.key is a separate file, and it is what decrypts stream keys, OAuth tokens and client secrets. Restore the database onto another machine without it and the install comes back looking healthy — every destination is listed, and every one of them is switched off, because its stream key cannot be read. Nothing on screen explains why, and the discovery happens at go-live. Back up both.
tour.dataDirectory.title: Back up secret.key with the database
tour.offerBody: A short tour of the things this console does not say out loud: where the publish address lives, what routing is actually for, and which file has to be backed up alongside the database. You can leave at any point, and start it again from Settings.
tour.offerDismissAria: Dismiss. The tour can be started again from Settings.
tour.publishUrl.body: This is what goes into the encoder. It stays empty until an ingest protocol is chosen for this source. The token underneath identifies the source; whether it also gates access depends on the ingest settings, and the note beside it says which is true on this install right now. Rotating issues a new token and keeps the old one working for five minutes, so a live encoder is not cut off mid-broadcast.
tour.publishUrl.title: The publish address, and the token
tour.renditionsNav.body: A rendition is one re-encode of the incoming feed — a resolution, a bitrate, an encoder — that several destinations can share, so one 1080p encode can feed three platforms instead of three separate encodes. Some controls on that page carry an experimental badge. It hides nothing and switches nothing off: it names one specific claim that has not been verified. There it is the command-line flags handed to NVENC, QSV, VA-API and AMF, which were read out of FFmpeg's own option tables and have never been watched producing an encode on real hardware. VideoToolbox is not in that set.
tour.renditionsNav.title: Renditions, and the experimental badge
tour.routingNav.body: A destination with no routing profile is plain restreaming, which every other tool does. A profile decides which incoming audio tracks reach which destination and how they are mixed: a commentary mic ducking a music bed for one platform, the music left out entirely for another, each with its own loudness target. It is set per destination, so one incoming feed can leave as several different programmes.
tour.routingNav.title: Routing is the part that is not restreaming
tour.sourcesNav.body: A source is one incoming feed, and this page is where its publish address and its token live. install.sh printed them once, when it ran; if that terminal has been closed, this is where to find them again. Each source carries its own token, so several encoders can publish to one install and stay apart.
